title: Rate-dilution grief still possible via cooldown (regression of v02 M-01)
description: A zero-stake EOA calls claim() (or any user path that invokes pullAndRefresh) every cooldown tick. Each call triggers dispatcherHook.pull() which returns small inflow, resetting windowEnd = now + windowDuration and recomputing rewardRate = rewardBudget / windowDuration. Because inflow per cooldown tick is almost always smaller than elapsed * rewardRate_old, each tick drags the emission rate toward the asymptote inflow_per_interval / windowDuration, well below the intended schedule, extending it indefinitely. Additionally, minPullInterval defaults to 0 in the constructor — between deployment and the first owner setMinPullInterval call, pre-fix behavior is fully active and the original M-01 attack works unrestricted. The v03 fix narrowed M-01's hard invariant to a weaker rate-limit that still admits the same attack at reduced throughput.
remediation: Reinstate the rate-monotonicity invariant at the mutation site, e.g., require(rewardRate >= rewardRate_pre || msg.sender == owner()) after recomputing rate. Or: skip the windowEnd/rewardRate rewrite when inflow < elapsed * rewardRate_old. Or: initialize minPullInterval to a non-zero value in the constructor and require it to remain non-zero.
poc_results: 2.04× rate collapse over 10,000 hourly ticks (~416 simulated days); honest staker loses 28.8% of intended emissions (2.399e21 wei phUSD); all 10,000 ticks strictly monotonic-decreasing. Default-interval scenario shows window reset on every one of 1,200 blocks.
